clue.text: Is it true? Trivially, a fantasy world generated by computer

indicators.note: letters generated from other letters are produced anew in a fresh order, so the fodder words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether something is real, and dismisses it as a trivial computer-made fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TRUE, TRIVIALLY and A are rearranged, with 'generated' as the signal; 'by computer' rounds out the definition's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulated environment created by software is the standard description of this technology.

clue.text: Trigger-happy terrorists sick in belief only odd characters allowed

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, is the usual crossword terrorist group

indicators.note: only the letters in odd-numbered positions of the run of words are kept, the even ones discarded

explanation.surface: A grumble about trigger-happy terrorists whose belief system tolerates only oddballs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'sick in belief' gives SCIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to fire off in anger is hot-tempered, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Annoyed by experiment on chromosome

parts.note: a test is an experiment
Y is the male sex chromosome

explanation.surface: A lab scientist irritated by an experiment on a chromosome.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts TEST above Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritable or short-tempered is a synonym for feeling annoyed.

clue.text: Worth, perhaps, gold in two islands or even more so

parts.note: Fort Worth in Texas, so Worth is an example of a fort: a fort

indicators.note: in places the gold inside the pair of island letters

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, twice
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A wealthy Texan city, perhaps with gold on two islands, is richer still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worth, perhaps' is a definition by example: Fort Worth makes Worth 'a fort'. OR sits between the two Is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in argument to mean with still stronger reason, i.e. all the more.

clue.text: Inflicts noise and offensive odours

indicators.note: noise signals that the word's sound, not its spelling, is wanted here

parts.note: to wreak havoc is to inflict it, so inflicts means wreaks

explanation.surface: Someone who brings both racket and bad smells on the neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong unpleasant smells are stinks, the plural noun sense of this word.

clue.text: Injured by dagger I've forged

indicators.note: something forged is hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A victim wounded by a dagger they claim to have made themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling wronged or hurt, especially in a legal sense of having suffered injury, is the meaning.

clue.text: Foul shot home and away

parts.note: being in means being at home
off means away, as in 'off on holiday'

explanation.surface: A footballer's foul shot, at home and away games alike.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and billiards the cue ball going into a pocket off another ball is a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, potting the cue ball after it strikes an object ball is penalised as a foul stroke.

clue.text: Root out no old-fashioned uprising of rebellious excolonists

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising sends the letters upward, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to root out is to seek
nay is an archaic word for no

explanation.surface: A call to stamp out an uprising by rebellious colonists, in old-fashioned style.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans, the colonists who rebelled against Britain, are nicknamed this, especially by the British.

clue.text: It is home for a doctor who travels backwards

definitions.text: It is home for a doctor who travels backwards

indicators.note: a home holds its occupant, so the contraction surrounds the other letters

parts.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is

indicators.note: travelling backwards means the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A description of a time-travelling doctor's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Doctor Who's time machine, which travels back in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who's police-box time machine is where the Doctor lives and travels through history.

clue.text: Gather a crowd

parts.note: a mass is a crowd of people

explanation.definitionFit: To collect or accumulate a great quantity is to gather it together.

clue.text: Wild balls receive an audible sigh

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls

indicators.note: audible means the word is heard rather than read, so its soundalike is entered

parts.note: a groan is a deep sigh of pain or dismay

explanation.surface: Wild deliveries make a bowler sigh out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden left to grow unchecked becomes rank and untamed, i.e. wild.

clue.text: Crack to produce tears in branch

indicators.note: in places the weeping inside the department abbreviation

parts.note: DEPT, department, is a branch of an organisation
to cry is to shed tears

explanation.surface: Someone breaking down in tears at the local branch office.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code is to work out the hidden message, which is to decode it.

clue.text: Cold, small river submerged two fish-heads

indicators.note: things submerged in a river sit inside it, so the river's letters surround them

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
the head of 'fish' is F, and two of them are FF

explanation.surface: A chilly scene of a small river with two fish heads sunk in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A runny nose with a minor head cold is called this, so the noun stands for the illness.

clue.text: South African support for Israeli

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A South African backing an Israeli cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is used for a Jew born in Israel, named after a local cactus fruit.

clue.text: Down below, a bat is dissected

indicators.note: a dissected thing is cut apart and laid out differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions from a biology lab: a bat on the bench below is being cut open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction to go with 'below', but it is the definition: depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being in a gloomy, depressed state, as the tide is at its lowest.

clue.text: Blind and bald Roman, 51, arrested

indicators.note: something arrested is held inside, so the plain word encloses the numeral

parts.note: a bald statement is plain, obvious
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A police report: a blind, bald Roman aged 51 was arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blind to something means being unaware of it, which is the sense here.

clue.text: The French soldiers, at the last minute, are put in force

parts.note: le is the French for the
GIs are American soldiers
late means at the last minute

explanation.surface: French troops arriving late are put into action.
explanation.definitionFit: To make law is to enact it, giving a rule legal effect.

clue.text: Issue from corrupt source

parts.note: food that has gone off is corrupted or spoiled
a spring is the source of a river

explanation.surface: A news story leaking out from a crooked informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a news matter, but it means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's issue, in legal language, means their children or descendants.

clue.text: Understands a supplement may show fluctuation

parts.note: to see something is to understand it
a wing is an extension added to a building

explanation.surface: Someone grasping that a supplement could reveal market swings.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving back and forth like a playground plank is to waver or swing repeatedly.

clue.text: Squeal from loose stones on church

parts.note: scree is loose stones on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: A shriek as loose stones fall onto a church roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill high-pitched cry, like that of brakes or an owl, is a squeal.

clue.text: Loud animal kept in stall

indicators.note: one thing kept in another sits inside it, so the animal's letters surround the musical letter

parts.note: a deer is an animal
F, forte, is loud in music

explanation.surface: A noisy beast confined in its stable stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stall' looks like a stable noun, but it is the verb: to put off.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay or postpone, the meaning of the verb here.

clue.text: Mostly raw part of meal?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, with its final letter cut off

parts.note: a dish is one course or part of a meal

explanation.surface: A salad item usually eaten uncooked as part of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a salad vegetable usually eaten uncooked.
explanation.definitionFit: This peppery root is a salad vegetable that is generally eaten uncooked.

clue.text: Suspects play with conkers

indicators.note: playing with something moves its parts about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children under suspicion of playing conkers, the British game of horse chestnuts on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect or suppose something is to judge or think it, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Religious singers lowered one in divine fluid

indicators.note: in a down clue lowering a letter moves it further down the word

parts.note: ichor is the fluid said to flow in the veins of the Greek gods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Church singers dipped into holy water.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of singers in a church service forms this body.

clue.text: For example Frankenstein's Shelley could improvise feverishly imaginative openings

indicators.note: the openings of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Mary Shelley, author of Frankenstein, could feverishly improvise imaginative opening chapters.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Frankenstein's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's novel is an early example of speculative fiction about science.

clue.text: What paparazzi did to saint got dropped off

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep, to nap

explanation.surface: Press photographers catching a saint nodding off.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers snatch quick pictures of celebrities, so taking such a shot is this verb.

clue.text: Helicopter dodges hospital at high speed

indicators.note: the helicopter dodges the letter, avoiding it, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: the Apache is a US attack helicopter

explanation.surface: An air ambulance swerving round a hospital at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving quickly or swiftly is the meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: A small coterie reinterpreted obscure knowledge

indicators.note: reinterpreted means the letters are read in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A little clique puts a new spin on arcane lore.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite facts known only to a few initiates are esoteric matters.

clue.text: They react when detectives are kidnapped

indicators.note: kidnapped people are held inside, so the word for when encloses the detectives

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives

explanation.surface: Something happens when the police detectives are abducted.
explanation.definitionFit: These chemicals react with bases and metals, so they are things that react.

clue.text: Callous urges could appear at breakfast-time

parts.note: hard-boiled means tough and unfeeling
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: Cruel impulses that might surface over breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly cooked eggs in their shells are a typical morning food.
